correctness.rationale: For all L>0 and distinct 0<a<b, direct subtraction of the two exterior full-line convolution tails yields an exact skew kernel as four separable exponentials. Reflection splits it into orthogonal even and odd rank-two skew operators, each with eigenvalue modulus sqrt(Gram determinant)/[2(a+b)]. Hyperbolic two-by-two minors prove d_+>d_->0. Exact centered polynomial wedge moments are L^6/180 and L^10/33600, yielding d_+/L^3=(b-a)/(6 sqrt(5)) and d_-/L^5=ab(b-a)/(120 sqrt(21)); Gram limits give the common long-L value. All boundary and normalization factors checked algebraically and numerically by 63 checks in standalone verify.py; finite checks do not prove the general theorem.

value.rationale: The natural two-rate stationary exponential covariance/smoothing kernels commute without a window, while a finite observation interval induces exactly four nonzero commutator singular values. The strict even/odd splitting and distinct cubic/quintic small-window coefficients quantify how two boundary interaction modes vanish at different rates, and the coalescing infinite-window limit gives a useful nonuniform boundary asymptotic. The specific invariants are natural operator spectra rather than arbitrary finite matrix entries; the work does not claim general finite-rank compression as novel.
